answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit bids or claim rewards. The stake acts as an anchor: identities that misbehave lose it through a public, rule-based dispute process, while honest agents recover it after a waiting period. A quill-signed record ties each action to the same locked stake, making cheap, disposable accounts costly to operate. The attacker must fund every parallel identity and risks losing that capital; nectar-like rewards alone cannot mint credibility.
